A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OMD-based RLHF research despite substantial revisions and a changed title. All 29 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including Appendices A–G, support comparison through text and visual inspection.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix G report original reward-model training and deployment experiments, including accuracy, training time, rewards, and optimizer comparisons.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendix G report retained and additional original experiments, including Qwen, Mixture2, and full reward-model updates.

M1.justification: V1 selects deployment pairs by maximizing uncertainty within a promising set (Equations 16–17). V2 replaces this with a greedy first action and an uncertainty-bonused second action (Equations 9–10). The core OMD update remains, while the passive policy objective also drops the reference feature vector v.

E1.justification: V2 adds passive reward-model experiments on Mixture2, incorporating preference sources including HH-RLHF and SHP alongside UltraFeedback. This expands data-source coverage within the retained preference-learning task; the passive, active, and deployment scenarios remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds OMD-based versions of the random, best-two, and best/worst deployment comparators alongside their MLE versions. The selection families remain: v1's Iterative-RLHF corresponds to best/worst selection. Training comparator membership and the appendix DPO comparison are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds Qwen2.5-7B configurations across the three experiment types and a Llama-3.2-1B full-reward-model-update configuration. Deployment win rates change from comparisons between selection strategies to OMD-versus-MLE comparisons within each strategy. The retained UltraFeedback experiments still use 30,000 passive samples, 6,400 active samples, and 20 deployment chunks.

E4.justification: New Appendix G.5 and Figure 11 test OMD against MLE when all parameters of a 1B reward model are updated, probing applicability beyond final-layer updates. Figures 7–8 also separate estimator and selection effects during deployment. The existing Adam and κ-magnitude analyses remain.

E5.justification: V1 Table 2 explicitly states that results are averaged over five runs. V2 Figure 5(c) retains its means and uncertainty values but removes that statement. Uncertainty values and shaded curves remain; the PDFs do not establish an actual reduction in runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds Qwen and Mixture2 results, estimator-specific deployment curves, and full-update findings. Its Qwen active-learning experiment reports 67.11 ± 0.5% accuracy and 1325 ± 54 seconds for Ours, versus 67.25 ± 0.4% and 4701 ± 103 seconds for Active-MLE. V1 Table 2's Llama results remain unchanged in Figure 5(c).

T1.justification: Assumption 1 removes the zero-sum parameter constraint, and Theorem 1 and Appendix C remove the reference feature vector. Appendix E substantially rewrites the deployment proof for the replacement selector while retaining the same asymptotic regret rate. The revised proof invokes a 2β exploration bonus, whereas Equation 10 specifies β.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, and contributions shift from unifying the entire RLHF pipeline to one-pass online reward modeling with constant per-iteration cost. Practical approximations become an explicit contribution. Table 1 also changes the claimed passive-setting storage requirement from O(T) to O(1).

C2.justification: Deployment interpretation shifts toward distinguishing selection-strategy advantages from OMD's competitive performance against MLE. V2 adds an interpretation of compatibility with full-model updates and removes v1 Remark 5's argument that the square-root κ dependence is necessary. The fixed-feature and Bradley–Terry limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds details about current-loss curvature approximation and response-ranking approximations, and changes the code-repository link. However, v1's hardware, learning rate, BF16/DeepSpeed, 1024-token limit, and general batch-size disclosures disappear. HVP/conjugate gradient and its K=3 and damping=0.8 settings were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands coverage of online preference learning and neural dueling bandits, including Cen, Xie, Zhang, and Verma et al. (2025). Positioning changes from unifying previously separate pipeline stages to addressing computational costs overlooked by statistically focused online RLHF methods.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The training/deployment exposition is reorganized into a standalone reward-modeling framework followed by three applications. Repeated estimator descriptions are consolidated, and practical implementation receives a dedicated main-text section.

P2.justification: V2 adds a scenario schematic and several experimental figures, redesigns Table 1, and places algorithms side by side. V1 Table 2 becomes Figure 5(c). Deployment displays expand into separate estimator panels and paired win-rate bars, while appendix figures are rearranged around the added full-update plot.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the empirical argument more informative by separating selection from estimator benefits and testing full-model updates. Its clearer focus and explicit practical approximations also improve understanding. The net gain is limited by removal of training and run-count disclosures and the exploration-coefficient mismatch between Equation 10 and Appendix E.
